content:
alex: Heads-up - jane.corp reported intermittent mTLS handshake failures to our Private control plane starting ~2026-03-17T10:20Z. Root log snippet shows TLS alert.

alex: logs: `2026-03-17T10:21:02Z controlplane tls: alert unknown_ca (40) during ClientHello -> handshake aborted`

jane.corp: yep, errors started after we rotated our intermediate CA yesterday. We run through a corporate egress proxy + strict allowlist.

jane.corp: here's what our ops saw from inside the proxy when we tried the connection: `tcp_reset` to remote IP immediately after SYN from client.

alex: quick ask - can you run `openssl s_client -connect controlplane.private.redwood:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -status -tls1_3` from a host behind your proxy and paste output? Need to see OCSP stapling behavior.

jane.corp: ran it, output below. Note: we anonymized IPs.

jane.corp: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = R3
verify return:1
OCSP response: no response sent
---
no peer certificate available
---
139584 bytes read
---
SSL handshake has read 139584 bytes and written 3222 bytes
Verification: OK
---
```

alex: interesting — OCSP response: no response sent. Our control plane cert is configured with Must-Staple and we expect the server (control plane) to staple OCSP; but the client (your side) also may try to fetch OCSP if stapled response missing. If your egress proxy/firewall blocks access to the OCSP responder (HTTP on port 80) or rewrites SNI, clients will fail validation or time out and trigger handshake failure.

ryan: adding infra note: We do staple OCSP in the control plane, but when there's an intermediate rotation it briefly relies on OCSP fetch paths for validation on client side. If the customer's egress denies outbound HTTP to ocsp responder host (or DNS for it), you'll see `no response sent` and then a client-side abort.

jane.corp: our allowlist only permits outbound to a set of IPs (api.whitelisted-ip, internal proxies) and blocks direct DNS resolution for external services. That would explain it. We tried `curl http://r3.o.lencr.org` from an internal host and got `Connection reset by peer` from the proxy.

alex: could you temporarily allow outbound HTTP (port 80) to the OCSP responder host(s) listed in the cert chain? Alternatively, allow full egress to the resolver used for the cert chain or add the OCSP responder FQDNs to your allowlist.

jane.corp: before we change policy — any safer mitigation? We can't open wide egress for hours.

ryan: short-term workaround: ensure your proxy passes `OCSP` by not intercepting/stopping the HTTP GET to the responder, or configure the proxy to whitelist the OCSP responder FQDNs. We can't disable Must-Staple on Redwood side. Another option: perform direct connectivity test from a bastion with a temporary more permissive policy and report back.

jane.corp: ok we added temporary allow rules for `r3.o.lencr.org` and `ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org` (the ones in our cert chain) and retried `openssl s_client -status`. New output: 

jane.corp: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = R3
verify return:1
OCSP Response: (status: successful)
    response status: successful
---
SSL handshake has read 3123 bytes and written 4122 bytes
Verification: OK
---
```

jane.corp: After allowlist tweak, our application-level mTLS connections now succeed. No more `unknown_ca` alerts in control plane.

alex: great — confirms egress allowlist was the culprit. I'll mark this as a customer environment config issue and add a note to our Private deployment checklist: call out OCSP responder FQDNs/IPs needed for certificate rotation and Must-Staple handling.

alex: action items: (1) jane.corp to keep allowlist changes in place or move to FQDN-based allowlist (2) ryan to add OCSP FQDNs to the Private docs firewall/egress section (3) support to follow up in 24h.

jane.corp: thanks team — will follow up once we move to a scoped FQDN allowlist. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall-bot: NOTE: created ticket INF-2026-453 to track doc update and add OCSP responder list to Private deployment docs.

alex: closing thread after 24h monitoring window. :white_check_mark:
